text: SUDBURY, Ont., March 6, 1902 - Smallpox has broken out in the lumber camps on the upper Spanish River, and the provincial health officer has placed three camps under strict quarantine. Eleven cases are reported, two of them fatal, among shantymen who came in from Quebec at Christmas. Guards have been posted on the tote road and no man may leave the limits without a certificate. A doctor and two nurses went up by sleigh yesterday with a supply of vaccine, and every man in the district is being vaccinated. The town council has fitted up an isolation hospital in an old boarding house on the edge of the town.
label: epidemic

text: Gastrointestinal illness outbreak at a ski resort staff residence near Banff, February 2012. About 140 employees ill with vomiting and diarrhea; norovirus confirmed.
label: epidemic

text: Infantile paralysis has struck Kindersley and the surrounding district, where 19 cases have been reported since the middle of July 1949, most of them children under ten. Two have died and four are in iron lungs at the Saskatoon hospital. The opening of school has been put off and the swimming pool is closed. Parents have been asked to keep children away from crowds.
label: epidemic

text: A cluster of bloody diarrhea cases reported by emergency departments in the Annapolis Valley in late August 1997 was traced to undercooked ground beef served at a church supper in a small Nova Scotia community. In all 34 people fell ill with E. coli O157:H7 infection; nine were admitted to hospital and two young children developed hemolytic uremic syndrome and needed dialysis in Halifax. Public health inspectors found that the burgers had been cooked on a grill that could not reach a safe temperature. The supplier's remaining stock was recalled, and the department issued an advisory on cooking ground meat thoroughly.
label: epidemic

text: Diphtheria at Morden, Man., November 1909. The school has been closed; there are 23 cases in the town and four children are dead.
label: epidemic

text: A tuberculosis survey carried out by a federal health team in the summer of 1955 found that the disease had spread rapidly through a settlement on the west coast of Hudson Bay. Of 312 people x-rayed, 41 showed active disease, and a further 60 were suspected cases. Several families had lost two or three members in as many years. Patients were sent south by aircraft and ship to sanatoria in Manitoba and Ontario, some to stay for more than a year. Nurses began a program of BCG vaccination for infants and young children, and the team recommended that a nursing station be built.
label: epidemic

text: Fifty-eight students at the University of Lethbridge caught mumps in the winter of 2014; most had received only one dose of vaccine, and booster clinics were held on campus.
label: epidemic

text: FORT FRANCES, Ont., Oct. 12, 1908 - The town is in the grip of an epidemic of typhoid fever, there being no fewer than eighty cases under treatment and seven deaths since the first of September. The cottage hospital is full and private houses have been turned into sick wards. The medical health officer lays the blame on the town water, drawn from the river below the point where several sewers empty, and has given orders that all drinking water be boiled. A supply of pure water is being brought in barrels from a spring three miles up the line.
label: epidemic

text: Scarlet fever, Lunenburg County, spring 1938: sixty cases among school children, and the rural schools of three districts closed for three weeks.
label: epidemic

text: In late October 2009 the second wave of pandemic H1N1 influenza reached a fly-in First Nation in northwestern Ontario. Within ten days the nursing station saw more than 200 people with influenza-like illness, out of a population of about 900. Eight patients, including a pregnant woman and two infants, were flown out to Thunder Bay and Winnipeg, and one elder died. The school and band office were closed, and the community cancelled a hockey tournament. A team of nurses flew in to run a vaccination clinic in the school gym, where more than 600 doses were given in three days.
label: epidemic

text: REGINA, Feb. 10, 1920 - A fresh outbreak of la grippe is reported from Weyburn and other towns in the south, where schools, churches and moving picture houses have once more been closed by order of the local boards of health. Doctors report over 300 cases in the district; the disease is said to be of a mild type, though there have been several deaths from pneumonia among the aged.
label: epidemic

text: An outbreak of infectious hepatitis at a children's summer camp on Lake Couchiching in July 1965 affected 37 campers and four counsellors. Health officers traced the source to a well near the camp kitchen that had been fouled by a leaking septic tank. The camp was closed for the season and all campers were given gamma globulin.
label: epidemic

text: In the spring of 1996 measles spread through a northern Alberta district where few children had been immunized: 46 cases, one child with encephalitis.
label: epidemic

text: QUEBEC, June 8, 1905 - The emigrant steamer Corinthia, which arrived at the quarantine station at Grosse Isle yesterday with 1,100 emigrants from Liverpool, has been detained there after the ship's surgeon reported three cases of smallpox in the steerage. The passengers are being landed on the island, bathed and vaccinated, and their baggage disinfected with sulphur. The sick have been removed to the isolation hospital. It is expected that the healthy passengers will be allowed to proceed to Montreal after fourteen days of observation.
label: epidemic

text: Five recruits died of cerebrospinal meningitis at a military training centre in western Canada in February 1941, and 23 more were admitted to hospital with the disease. The camp was put under quarantine for three weeks and all leave was cancelled. Medical officers ordered that the beds in the barrack huts be spaced six feet apart and that windows be kept open at night despite the cold. The men were given sulfa drugs as a precaution. The outbreak was reported to have begun with a draft that had arrived from the east.
label: epidemic

text: Legionnaires' disease outbreak, Brandon, Manitoba, August 2001: 14 cases among people who had been in the downtown area; one death. The source was traced to a contaminated cooling tower on the roof of a commercial building, which was disinfected and shut down.
label: epidemic

text: Measles has broken out in the settlements north of Yorkton, 1904; seventy children ill and the schools closed.
label: epidemic

text: Whooping cough has swept through a Newfoundland outport on the south coast this winter, February 1950, and the nurse reports that 42 children have had the disease, three of whom have died. A doctor came in on the coastal boat with vaccine, and the families have been told to keep children with the cough away from babies.
label: epidemic

text: A COVID-19 outbreak declared at a long-term care home in a small Manitoba town on 2 November 2020 grew to 61 resident cases and 37 staff cases within three weeks. Seventeen residents died. So many staff were ill or isolating that the Canadian Red Cross was called in to help with care. Families were barred from visiting and the home's residents were confined to their rooms.
label: epidemic

text: MORRIS, Man., May 28, 1923 - The receding waters of the Red River have left behind a crop of typhoid fever. Eighteen cases have been reported in the town and the surrounding district, where wells and cisterns were fouled by the flood. The provincial board of health has sent a nurse and has ordered every well tested; meanwhile all water is to be boiled. One death, that of a young girl, is reported.
label: epidemic

text: Thirty-one cases of poliomyelitis and three deaths had been reported in the Lakehead by the end of August 1952; swimming beaches and wading pools were closed.
label: epidemic

text: Public health investigation summary: between January and June 2016, 22 cases of active pulmonary tuberculosis were identified among clients and staff of an emergency shelter in a western Canadian city. Genotyping showed that all cases shared the same strain. Contact tracing reached more than 600 people, and about 180 were started on treatment for latent infection. The investigation found that poor ventilation in the overnight sleeping rooms and the long delay before ill clients were seen by a doctor had allowed the disease to spread. The health authority installed ultraviolet germicidal lights and began routine screening of shelter users.
label: epidemic

text: WINNIPEG, Jan. 15, 1910 - Three new cases of smallpox were found yesterday in the north end, bringing the total for the month to twenty-six. Houses where the disease appears are placarded and the inmates removed to the isolation hospital. Free vaccination will be given at the city hall every afternoon this week.
label: epidemic

text: Influenza reached the schools of the Ottawa Valley in the first week of October 1962, and on some days a third of the pupils were absent. In Pembroke, two schools closed for a week and the teachers themselves fell ill. Doctors were making as many as sixty house calls a day. Most cases were mild, with fever and aches lasting three or four days, but the hospital admitted several elderly patients with pneumonia and four of them died. Vaccine was in short supply and was given first to doctors, nurses and hospital staff.
label: epidemic

text: About 80 guests fell ill and five were admitted to hospital after a catered wedding reception near Moncton in July 2005. Salmonella was found in the chicken salad.
label: epidemic

text: EDSON, Alta., Sept. 1911 - Typhoid fever has broken out among the construction gangs on the new line west of here, and the camp hospital at the end of steel is crowded. Thirty-four men are down with the fever and six have died. The camps were placed near a slough which serves as both water supply and sewer, and the government inspector has ordered the camp moved to higher ground.
label: epidemic

text: German measles has been unusually common in the Maritimes this spring of 1971, with more than 1,000 cases reported to the health department in New Brunswick alone. Doctors are warning that expectant mothers who catch the disease early in pregnancy risk having babies with defects of the eyes, ears and heart, and some obstetricians have asked their patients to stay away from children's gatherings.
label: epidemic

text: Hepatitis A outbreak linked to an infected food handler at a restaurant in Kelowna, May 2018. Health officials offered vaccine to about 3,000 diners; eleven cases confirmed.
label: epidemic

text: BRANDON, 1903 - Scarlet fever is spreading in the east ward, and the yellow quarantine card now hangs on some forty houses. Two children have died.
label: epidemic

text: In September 1996, the medical health officer for a Kootenay village of 1,800 people issued a boil-water order after 23 residents were confirmed to have giardiasis, an intestinal parasite infection, and dozens more reported stomach illness. The village drew its water from an unfiltered creek. Investigators believed beaver activity upstream and heavy rains in late August had contaminated the intake. Bottled water was handed out at the community hall, and the village applied for funding to install a filtration plant. The advisory was lifted after four months.
label: epidemic
